provenance.quote: Newark Essential Services Protection Measure. To protect city services such as repairing potholes/streets; keeping neighborhoods safe/clean, and maintaining 9-1-1 emergency response/fire protection/neighborhood police patrols/parks/recreation programs, shall the measure be adopted updating Newark’s 56-year-old business license ordinance, lowering many small businesses’ taxes, with rates up to 0.3% of gross receipts (as described in the ordinance), raising $6,600,000 annually until ended by voters, with spending disclosure/independent audits?

provenance.quote: Newark Essential Services Protection Measure. To protect city services such as repairing potholes/streets; keeping neighborhoods safe/clean, and maintaining 9-1-1 emergency response/fire protection/neighborhood police patrols/parks/recreation programs, shall the measure be adopted updating Newark’s 56-year-old business license ordinance, lowering many small businesses’ taxes, with rates up to 0.3% of gross receipts (as described in the ordinance), raising $6,600,000 annually until ended by voters, with spending disclosure/independent audits?

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Replaces Newark’s business-license tax ordinance beginning January 1, 2027. Taxable businesses would pay a $25 base tax on their first $100,000 of annual gross receipts—business revenue before expenses—or any portion of that amount, plus a category rate on receipts above $100,000. Those rates range from $0.30 to $3 per $1,000 above the threshold. The measure includes qualifying exemptions, public spending disclosure and annual independent audits. Estimated revenue is $6.6 million a year for any lawful city purpose. It requires majority approval and has no fixed expiration.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Adopt the replacement business-license ordinance, $25 base tax and category rates on receipts above $100,000, with eligible exemptions and accountability requirements.
measureRecords.noMeans: Keep the existing business-license tax ordinance and structure.

parts.label: Category rates above $100,000
parts.what: In addition to the $25 base tax, general retail and restaurants pay $0.30 per $1,000; professional services pay $2.50; contractors and services pay $2; commercial and residential rentals, self-storage, hotels, motels and short-term rentals pay $0.75; manufacturing, wholesale and import/export businesses pay $0.75; and distribution and logistics pay $3. These rates apply only to receipts above $100,000. Businesses not clearly classified, or reasonably fitting more than one category, are classified as services. The distribution category excludes self-storage.

parts.label: Exemptions
parts.what: Qualifying not-for-profit entities, banks, insurance companies other than brokers, agriculture except associated retail, and specified events benefiting a local church, school or benevolent purpose are exempt but generally need a free tax-exempt certificate and annual eligibility application. Other exemptions cover government-owned utilities and public districts, certain regulated transportation vehicles, and occasional deliveries by outside-city businesses; after four deliveries in twelve months, further deliveries are no longer treated as occasional. Federal and state tax exemptions remain protected.

parts.label: Registration, payment and adjustments
parts.what: Separate certificates are required for each branch or location, except incidental warehouses or distribution sites connected with a taxed business. Certificates last at most twelve months. Tax is due when issued and annually afterward, becoming delinquent after thirty days. Late tax carries a 20% initial penalty and another 20% each later calendar month, capped at 50% of the tax due. New businesses estimate receipts, then report actual receipts within thirty days after the covered period; the minimum tax is paid in advance without proration. Refund claims must be made within one year after payment.

parts.label: Classification reviews and council authority
parts.what: The ordinance provides classification and reclassification reviews, with a ten-working-day request period for a council hearing on a reclassification decision and a separate fifteen-day appeal period for a classification decision to a hearing officer. Reclassification applies prospectively and no more than once a year. The collector may extend a filing deadline by up to sixty days for good cause. The council may amend or repeal the ordinance within its authority, but rate or calculation changes that increase a person’s tax require voters. It may restore a previously reduced rate up to the approved rate.
